topic: How did Lord Shaftesbury help to change the lives of children?
rationaleNote: This overview earns one sheet because Lesson 5 can point back to the concrete work-and-learning changes, their reach and their limits when children explain later changes in childhood. Separate misconception and vocabulary sheets were cut because they do not add a distinct recurring job.

cards.title: Why Shaftesbury mattered
cards.heroCaption: Lord Shaftesbury campaigned with others to protect children through laws.

groups.title: Work
items: The 1842 Mines Act banned underground work for women, girls and boys under ten.
Boys aged ten and over could still work underground.

groups.title: Learning
items: Shaftesbury supported ragged schools, where volunteer teachers gave poorer children free lessons.
In 1944, long after his death, the charity supporting ragged schools changed its name from the Ragged School Union to the Shaftesbury Society.
